text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cont-batcher latency & KV-cache eviction surge detected in us-west-2. Paging threshold breached for pool `cb-pool-7`. Possible continuous-batching misconfig or hot key causing cache amplification. Notifying @maya (oncall).
maya: on it, thanks. any customer 5xx spikes or is it internal timeouts? give me TOP metrics (evictions/s, avg latency, batch sizes).
liam: seeing customer 500s for 2 tenants (acme-inc, bluebird). spike started ~3345678920. 500s correlate with `cache_miss_error` and `batch_timeout`. Rough numbers: evictions ~120/s (baseline 2/s), p95 latency from 180ms -> 1600ms, error rate 2.4% -> 18%.
anna: pulling logs now. snippet from cont-batcher node-3:
```
[3345678931] WARN evictor.cpp: kv page thrash detected for shard=15, evict_count=98
[3345678935] ERROR batch_dispatch.cpp: batch timed out after 1500ms, seqs=24 tokens=13000
[3345678940] INFO kvcache: rewarm queued, backpressure=HIGH
```
anna: also saw a sudden config drift on one of the config managers — `max_batch_tokens` was set to `16384` on cb-pool-7 (should be 4096). looks like a bad rollout earlier today.
maya: ok, that explains token-heavy batches + high seq counts -> eviction amplification. immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 2048 and `max_num_seqs` to 8 for cb-pool-7, 2) increase `timeout_ms` to 1200 -> avoid catastrophic timeouts, 3) enable fallback routing to model-variant `gpt-small-quant` for affected customers, 4) notify CS. can someone execute the config patch? @liam?
liam: on it. pushing patch to canary then pool. running patch command now.
devops-bot: Runbook step 3 triggered by liam — applying runtime config patch to pool `cb-pool-7` (canary first). Command:
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap contbatch-config-cb-pool-7 -p '{"data":{"max_batch_tokens":"2048","max_num_seqs":"8","timeout_ms":"1200"}}'
```
devops-bot: canary applied to node-12. monitoring started.
liam: canary metrics look good after ~30s. evictions -> 6/s, p95 latency -> 320ms, batch sizes reduced. rolling patch to remaining nodes now.
deploy-bot: rollout started: cont-batcher-config/cb-pool-7 -> 8 nodes, strategy=rolling, grace=10s
liam: rollout complete, metrics stabilizing. error rate down to 0.6% for those tenants. still seeing elevated rewarm queue but manageable.
anna: one oddity: a backlog of rewarm requests caused an intermediate spike in IO at 3345679055; we throttled rewarm workers to 4 threads which helped. command used:
```
echo 4 > /sys/fs/contbatch/rewarm_workers
```
emily-cs: ping — I notified the two affected customers (acme-inc, bluebird) at 3345679068, they saw degraded responses and raised support tickets. acme reported degraded UX but no data loss. they've accepted the temporary fallback to `gpt-small-quant`.
maya: good. short-term mitigation done. next steps: - open INC ticket linking to this thread and metrics dashboards - schedule rollback check: revert to previous intended config (max_batch_tokens=4096) only after controlled canary and validation - RCA to investigate why rollout drifted to 16384 (CI/CD guardrails?) - add automatic config-sanity alert to detect >2x changes to batch token limits
liam: creating INC-3345679 and linking dashboards + grafana panels. will add the faulty config commit hash and who triggered it.
anna: collecting heap/disk traces from node-3 to see if rewarm left stale pages; will attach to INC.
maya: handoff: @maya -> night-oncall (alex) in 30m. alex, please watch evictions and rewarm queue for next 4 hours, and if error rate >1% for >5m, rollback contbatch continuous-batching to `disabled` for cb-pool-7. I'll write runbook step and checklist in INC.
alex (automated-handoff): :wave: acknowledged handoff. monitoring alert set. thanks team.
maya: thanks everyone — great quick ops. follow-ups: postmortem in 72h, config guardrails item assigned to infra team, CS to confirm customers comfortable with SLA credit if needed. :thumbsup:
